newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kuwait cuts term naphtha premium to $18 -- traders.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait cuts term naphtha premium to $18 -- traders.

text.p: In term naphtha talks between Kuwait and its Asian clients, Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) has cut its offer price to $18.00 per tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes from its previous offer of $20.00, traders said on Tuesday.

Following the notification of the revised offer price for one-year term supply contracts starting in August, KPC also told potential buyers that some firms in term negotiations have already accepted the new offer price, one trader said.
If KPC sticks to the policy of "one price for one commodity," the rest of the buyers in the talks will eventually have to accept the new number, he said.
Term premiums for KPC cargoes were set at $7.90 for annual supply contracts that started in August 1996, and at $13.50 for those starting in March 1997.
Japan and South Korea are expected to import around two million tonnes of Kuwaiti material in the new term year, traders said.
